messages.content: Use web search to find relevant datasets. Only include landing pages or DOIs. Do not invent links. Do not call time, date, timestamp, or clock tools.

Query: Can you find datasets about Media in German Democratic Republic (1949-1990) during the 1980s, matching this research need: Survey data on TV viewing participation and program evaluations, including audience reactions to police drama episodes, Saturday evening entertainment, music shows, children’s summer holiday viewing, preferred viewing times, and related demographics.
Respond ONLY as JSON in this exact shape: {"items":[{"title":"...","url_or_doi":"...","justification":"..."}]}. Put any DOI, URL, landing page, or link in url_or_doi.

content.text: {"items":[{"title":"Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 36. Woche 1985 (SFR 36/85)","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA7189","justification":"Highly relevant survey dataset from 1985 examining television viewing participation and program evaluations in the German Democratic Republic. Includes audience reactions to the police drama POLIZEIRUF 110 – EIN SCHRITT ZU WEIT, specifically its suspense, entertainment value, perceived realism, and fulfillment of viewer expectations. Also evaluates other television films and sports programs. Based on a representative household sample, with demographic information suitable for analyzing differences between viewer groups."},{"title":"Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 35. Woche 1988 (SFR 35/88)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.10584","justification":"Excellent match for research on audience reactions to police dramas and entertainment programming. This 1988 DDR television survey evaluates the POLIZEIRUF 110 episode EIFERSUCHT, including entertainment value, realism, audience appreciation of main characters, and specific narrative elements. It also examines audience evaluations of the entertainment show GLÜCK MUSS MAN HABEN, including its host, humor, participating couples, and program components. Contains weekly viewing participation and program ratings collected through representative household sampling."},{"title":"Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 13. Woche 1985 (SFR 13/85)","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA7166","justification":"Directly relevant to evaluations of police drama episodes and preferred television scheduling. The survey investigates audience reactions to POLIZEIRUF 110 – TRAUM DES VERGESSENS, including suspense, perceived realism, and whether the episode met expectations. Additional questions explore interest in cultural programming, preferred broadcast days, viewing frequency, working conditions, fatigue after work, and expectations of television entertainment. Useful for studying relationships between viewing preferences, employment circumstances, and audience demographics."},{"title":"Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 50. Woche 1982 (SFR 50/82)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.7047","justification":"Particularly relevant to Saturday evening entertainment and music programming in the early 1980s. Contains weekly television viewing participation and program evaluations, including audience assessments of KLOCK 8, ACHTERN STROM, its humor and entertainment value, suggestions for improvement, and preferences for suitable Saturday evening programming. Also examines viewing and evaluations of the musical series BUSCH SINGT, preferred broadcast days for VERKEHRSKOMPASS, and television viewing opportunities during holidays. Includes demographic variables for audience segmentation."},{"title":"Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 39. Woche 1982 (SFR 39/82)","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA7464?lang=en","justification":"Strong match for research on Saturday evening entertainment and music shows. Includes questions evaluating whether coverage of an international Schlager music festival was appropriate for Saturday evening television. Also examines audience assessments of the entertainment production KOMM MIT MIR NACH CHICAGO, including relaxation, enjoyment, character identification, representation of young people's experiences, and overall impressions. Further questions evaluate the quiz show KNOBELEIEN, its presenters, format, and studio games. Provides valuable evidence on viewer preferences and entertainment program reception in the DDR."},{"title":"Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 28. Woche 1989 (SFR 28/89)","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA7389","justification":"Relevant survey dataset covering television participation, program evaluations, and music entertainment near the end of the DDR. Includes audience ratings of performers and the host of SHOWKOLADE, reception of PFUNDGRUBE, evaluations of a presenter, and satisfaction with the diversity of musical offerings. Also examines general satisfaction with DDR television programming and other cultural and informational content. Particularly useful for studying audience preferences for music shows, presenter appeal, and entertainment formats."},{"title":"Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 46. Woche 1984 (SFR 46/84)","url_or_doi":"https://doi.org/10.4232/1.7147","justification":"Especially relevant to preferred viewing times, household viewing practices, and demographic influences on television consumption. Includes questions about desired broadcast times for a new youth television program, parental influence on children's viewing behavior, knowledge of television schedules, and the effects of shift work on viewing opportunities. Also measures weekly program participation and evaluations. Demographic variables include age, gender, education, employment, household size, and political affiliation. Particularly valuable for investigating how social and occupational characteristics shaped television preferences."},{"title":"Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 6. Woche 1983 (SFR 6/83)","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA7055?lang=de","justification":"Relevant to entertainment programming, musical and cultural formats, and age-specific audience preferences. Investigates evaluations of the youth-oriented program BONG, including entertainment value, presenter appeal, and perceived target age group. Also examines regular viewing and evaluations of KLOCK 8, ACHTERN STROM, audience opinions about program improvements, and attitudes toward scheduling entertainment across different weekdays. Suitable for studying age-related preferences and audience responses to entertainment formats."},{"title":"Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 14. Woche 1982 (SFR 14/82)","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA7012?lang=en","justification":"Useful supplementary dataset on television participation, entertainment evaluations, and program awareness in the DDR. Includes audience assessments of DER STAATSANWALT HAT DAS WORT: HOFFNUNG FÜR ANNA, focusing on realism, entertainment value, and perceived crime-prevention effects. Also investigates the reception of television drama, awareness of youth-oriented programming, and viewing of recurring television series. Provides comparative material for studying audience responses to crime-related fictional television and other program genres."},{"title":"Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 23. Woche 1987 (SFR 23/87)","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA7281?lang=de","justification":"Relevant to audience evaluations of entertainment programs, films, presenters, and television content. Includes assessments of the entertainment show WENNSCHON – DENNSCHON, particularly its presenter, featured records, and informational value. Also examines viewers' reactions to films, characters, realism, and program themes. The survey records weekly viewing participation and program evaluations and uses representative household sampling. Useful for comparative analysis of entertainment preferences during the late 1980s."},{"title":"Sofortresonanzen DDR Fernsehen 5. Woche 1985 (SFR 5/85)","url_or_doi":"https://search.gesis.org/research_data/ZA7158?lang=en","justification":"Useful for investigating television viewing as a household and family activity. Includes questions about reasons for watching AUF SCHUSTERS RAPPEN, evaluations of its presenter, conversations with family members during television programs and films, and assessments of entertainment value and interesting program elements. Also records weekly viewing participation and program evaluations. Offers supplementary evidence for studying social viewing practices, audience engagement, and demographic differences."}]}
